header.name: Learning and Memory
header.description: The course will introduce the students to the stages and mechanisms by which environmental information is learned;how it  flows from sensory receptors through sensory, short- term to long-term memory, its storage and retrieval. Lectures and discussions will draw from published scientific evidence mainly in the areas of behaviour, neuroimaging and neurophysiology to elucidate the organization and implementation of memory in the brain that influences various aspects of human cognition. An additional component will involve computational analysis of experimental datasets in this field to draw brain-behaviour inferences pertaining to learning and memory. The course will engage students to develop analytical thinking based on experimental data towards building capacity for original ideation in this area of cognitive science that is relatable to science and technology.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Describe historical antecedents, cognitive science methods for studying learning and memory.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Explain Habituation, Sensitization, Familiarization with their mechanisms.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Classify and explain the basic mechanisms of Learning,  Short and Long term Memory, Forgetting.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students can  deconstruct data and draw conclusions from experiment(s) in learning and memory.

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: Utilize the afrometioned concepts to generate and articulate one experimentally testable idea in learning and memory.

lecture_topics: Approaches for the Study of Learning and Memory
Concept of Memory and its relation to Brain
